1.1. BIDS MUST BE SUBMITTED ELECTRONICALLY BY THE STIPULATED TIME TO THE LINK

5.1 Participation in the tender process is subject to compliance with the rules contained in this RFP 
Part C. 
5.2 All persons (whether a participant in this tender process or not) having obtained or received this 
RFP may only use it, and the information contained herein, in compliance with the rules contained 
in this RFP. 
5.3 All Bidders are deemed to accept the rules contained in this RFP Part C. 
5.4 The rules contained in this RFP Part C apply to: 
5.4.1 The RFP and any other information given, received or made available in connection 
with this RFP, and any revisions or annexure. 
5.4.2 the Tendering Process; and 
5.4.3 any communications (including any briefings, presentations, meetings and 
negotiations) relating to the RFP or the Tendering Process.

any person(s), or as creating any form of contractual, promissory or other rights .  No binding 
contract or other understanding for the supply of services will exist between the DBSA and any 
Bidder unless and until the DBSA has executed a formal written contract with the successful 
Bidder.

no representations or warranties that the content in this RFP or any information communicated to 
or provided to Bidders during the Tendering Process is, or will be, accurate, current or complete.

No representations made by or on behalf of the DBSA in relation to this RFP will be binding on the

between the DBSA and the successful Bidder.

connection with this RFP or the Tendering Process must keep the contents of the RFP and other 
such information confidential, and not disclose or use the information except as required for the 
purpose of developing a proposal in response to this RFP.

Officer.

issued in connection with the Tendering Process must be submitted to the Tender Officer in writing, 
and most preferably by e-mail to kgomotsoscm@dbsa.org  
11.3 Any communication by a Bidder to the DBSA will be effective upon receipt by the Tender Officer

1. INTRODUCTION  
The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies (DCDT), the South African Post Office 
(SAPO) and the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) are collaborating to translate SAPO’s 
Business Rescue (BR) Implementation Approach into a practical route to delivery. The DBSA seeks an 
independent consulting firm (the “Service Provider”) to validate the inputs received on the Request for 
Information (RFI) issued by DCDT and SAPO on the 14 November  2025, rationalise and bundle the 
most credible initiatives, classify SAPO assets into core and non ‑core categories, and prepare a 
business case with a bankable implementation plan  and indicative costing model that can be executed 
over the next phase. 
 
2. BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT 
The SAPO is undergoing a critical phase of organisational restructuring and renewal following a 
prolonged period of financial instability and operational decline. As SAPO prepares to exit Business 
Rescue phase, there is a clear strategic intent to reposition the entity as a modernised, hybrid logistics 
and digital services platform capable of driving inclusive service delivery across the country in line with 
their mandate as provided for in the South African Post Office Act 22 of 2011 as amended by 2024 
Amendment Act, the Postal Services Act 124 of 1998 and related Regulations. This intention is explicitly 
reflected in the RFI issued on 14 November 2025, which signals SAPO’s move to leverage underutilised 
assets, optimise its infrastructure footprint, and restore its role as a national enabler of postal, logistics, 
e-commerce, financial inclusion, and e-government services.
